source.notes: Phase 5c recapture: refreshed `tithiEndsAt` on all 84 cases and re-rendered the one timestamp that was not on the +05:30 convention. Old results: `tithiEndsAt` still came from the Phase 2 capture, when the transition was bisected to 1 minute, so the six cities stored different instants for the same global event - spreads of 10-50 s (2026-01-14: 12:23:24Z .. 12:24:14Z). That noise used most of the 60 s tolerance, so the field could barely detect a real regression. New results: every `tithiEndsAt` is the shared crossing solver output, and cases that share a sunrise tithi now agree to the second. `delhi-1800-01-01` `moonrise` was rendered at LMT `+05:53` (truncated from the zone's +05:53:28), the only value in the file outside the stated convention; the instant is unchanged, it is now written as `+05:30` like every other timestamp. Reason: the fixture is a regression lock, and a 50 s capture-era spread inside a 60 s tolerance is not a lock. No astronomical value changed; the 19 s move on the 1800 moonrise is the truncated-offset parse error, not a new calculation. Phase 5b recapture: added `nakshatraStartsAt`, `nakshatraEndsAt`, `nextNakshatra` and `nextSankranti` to all 84 cases and bumped `schemaVersion` 1 -> 2. Old result: the four fields did not exist, so the sunrise nakshatra's edges and the next solar ingress had no regression lock. New result: edges from the shared crossing solver through `resolveNakshatraSpan` (the same path `nakshatraTimingsProvider` uses), and the ingress from `findSankrantiInstant` (first solar sign crossing strictly after sunrise, searched within 40 days). Reason: Phase 3 moved every edge onto one solver and nothing locked the nakshatra span or the Sankranti instant, so a regression there could only surface as a wrong "Rohini until 3:42 PM" or a wrong Bengali month. No existing value changed. The ingress instants are engine characterization, not an accuracy claim: a cross-check of the Mesha ingress on 2026-04-14 gives 09:30:15 IST here against a published 09:39, the ~9 minute ayanamsa variant that the fixture already carries elsewhere. Phase 5 recapture of every `moonrise` value. Profile change: lunar rise/set moved from the truncated pure-Dart lunar series (MoonriseCalculator, ~0.3 deg longitude, bisected to 1 minute) to native `swe_rise_trans` (topocentric, true ecliptic latitude, PanchangProfile.standard = upper limb + standard refraction). Old results were whole-minute approximations; new results are native to the second and differ by -120 s to +120 s (27 of 83 cases moved more than the 60 s tolerance, the rest by under a minute). Reason: moonrise decides Karva Chauth's puja and paran, so the observance path may not use an approximation. No other field changed; sunrise, sunset, tithi ends and the tithi/nakshatra/yoga/karana/masa values are untouched. Prior history: Phase 2 recapture after panchang-v3 replaced the night-midpoint Nishita sample with the Nishita window (sunset + 7/15 night to + 8/15 night, microsecond edges), plus the Boishakh-1 month-start fix (2026-04-14 is Choitro 30, 1432 and 2026-04-15 cases were added). Regression lock only; not an external accuracy certification.

Janmashtami defect fixed by panchang-v3: the tithi is now sampled at the Nishita window opening (sunset + 7/15 night = 23:57:19) instead of the night midpoint (00:20), where the raw tithi is 24.005 (Navami). Ashtami (raw 23.987) prevails at the opening, so this day resolves janmashtami. Old result: []. New result: ["janmashtami"]. See docs/jyotish_package_improvements_plan.md, Phase 2.

Decided by seconds, recorded as-is: Ashtami ends at 00:14:06 and the Nishita window (sunset + 7/15 night to + 8/15 night) opens at 00:14:11, so Ashtami prevails at neither edge and panchang-v3 resolves no janmashtami on this date (Navami at the opening, raw 24.0001). The pre-v3 note claimed Ashtami still prevailed because it compared minute-rounded times from the Phase 0 capture (Ashtami end 00:14:36); the native Hindu sunrise/sunset moved the window edge past the boundary by ~6 s. Old result: [] (midpoint sample). New result: [] (window edges). Kept as a documented boundary case, not an external accuracy claim; see docs/jyotish_package_improvements_plan.md, Phase 2.

Bengali date corrected from {1433, Boishakh, 1} to {1432, Choitro, 30}: West Bengal Poila Boishakh 1433 is 2026-04-15, because Mesha sankranti falls at 09:39 IST on 2026-04-14 and the Bengal rule gives the sankranti civil day to the outgoing month (Drik Panchang, Indian Express, Times of India; Prokerala and Hindupad give Choitro 1432 as Mar 16 - Apr 14). The Panchang fields remain engine characterization.
